question: In the radiation-associated sarcoma cohort, which driver alteration dominates RT-angiosarcoma of the breast/chest wall, and at what frequency?
gold_notes: MYC amplification, 87% of 38 breast cases (75% of all 40 RT-AS).

rag.answer:
Based on the passages, **MYC amplification** dominates radiation-associated angiosarcoma (RT-AS) of the breast/chest wall, occurring at a frequency of **87%** (PMID:37350195).

Specifically, the study found that "All 33 RT-AS cases that were MYC amplified were from the breast/chest wall with a history of breast carcinoma (87% of 38 cases)" (PMID:37350195). This MYC amplification is notably site-specific: "Consistent with previous findings, MYC amplification was seen in 87% of RT-AS from the breast/chest wall in patients with a history of breast carcinoma, while no amplifications were detected in RT-AS occurring at other sites" (PMID:37350195).
